sections.heading: Implicit differentiation with logarithmic and exponential terms

questions.q: Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for $e^y=xy$.
Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for $\ln(x+y)=x^2$.
Find all points on the curve $x^2+xy+y^2=7$ where the tangent line is horizontal.
questions.answer: Differentiate: $2x+y+x\frac{dy}{dx}+2y\frac{dy}{dx}=0$: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{-2x-y}{x+2y}$. Horizontal tangent needs $-2x-y=0$, i.e. $y=-2x$. Substituting into the curve: $x^2+x(-2x)+(-2x)^2=7 \Rightarrow x^2-2x^2+4x^2=7 \Rightarrow 3x^2=7 \Rightarrow x=\pm\sqrt{7/3}$. Points: $\left(\pm\sqrt{7/3},\mp2\sqrt{7/3}\right)$.

questions.q: Find the points on the circle $x^2+y^2=9$ where the tangent line is vertical (i.e. where $\frac{dx}{dy}=0$, or equivalently where $\frac{dy}{dx}$ is undefined).
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{x}{y}$ is undefined when $y=0$. Substituting into the circle: $x^2=9$, so $x=\pm3$. Vertical tangents occur at $(3,0)$ and $(-3,0)$.

sections.heading: Implicit differentiation in an applied context

questions.q: A conical tank has height and radius related by $h=2r$ at all times as it fills, so its volume is $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2(2r)=\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3$. Using implicit differentiation with respect to time, find $\frac{dV}{dt}$ in terms of $r$ and $\frac{dr}{dt}$.
questions.answer: Differentiating both sides with respect to $t$: $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{2}{3}\pi(3r^2)\frac{dr}{dt}=2\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}$.

questions.q: Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for the curve $x^2y^2+xy=6$ at the point $(1,2)$.
Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for $\cos(x-y)=y\sin x$.
questions.answer: Differentiate: $-\sin(x-y)\left(1-\frac{dy}{dx}\right)=\frac{dy}{dx}\sin x+y\cos x$: $-\sin(x-y)+\sin(x-y)\frac{dy}{dx}=\sin x\frac{dy}{dx}+y\cos x$. Collecting terms: $\frac{dy}{dx}\left[\sin(x-y)-\sin x\right]=y\cos x+\sin(x-y)$, so $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y\cos x+\sin(x-y)}{\sin(x-y)-\sin x}$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=2x^3+x-5$ is one-to-one and differentiable, find $(f^{-1})'(-2)$, first identifying the input $a$ such that $f(a)=-2$.
For the hyperbola $xy=6$, complete each step:
parts: Confirm your answer matches what you'd get by first solving for $y=\frac{6}{x}$ and differentiating directly.
answers: Direct: $y=6x^{-1}$, so $\frac{dy}{dx}=-6x^{-2}=-\frac{6}{x^2}$. Substituting $y=\frac{6}{x}$ into $-\frac{y}{x}$: $-\frac{6/x}{x}=-\frac{6}{x^2}$. Both match.
